races.name: Ballylinch Stud Irish EBF Ingabelle Stakes (Listed)

runners_data.name: Timeless Tale
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in one start over 6f on Good, steps up to 7f here for W McCreery with W J Lee aboard; prominent style is perfectly calibrated for a race with three front-runners to stalk, and the McCreery T14 figure of 4/22 is respectable — the horse to beat on Strand Scorecard.

runners_data.name: Lady Patrona
runners_data.note: Five career starts show plenty of experience for a juvenile with 1W3P on Good, though her front-running role in a three-way early battle is a concern for stamina reserves; quick 7-day turnaround for Mrs Harrington warrants monitoring.

runners_data.name: Maeda Matsu
runners_data.note: Unbeaten juvenile with two wins including a 7f success on Good — her form is rock solid, but she is a genuinely prominent-style horse who is likely to find herself racing further back than she wants given the three dedicated leaders already present, blunting her usual weapon.

runners_data.name: Miss Cashman Hooke
runners_data.note: One run, a fourth over 6f on Good, provides very limited evidence; a natural midfield operator with Ben Coen up, her chance depends on a punishing pace creating late opportunities — unexposed but unproven at this level.

runners_data.name: Apollo's Comet
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Good and placed over the same trip, so trip and going are fine; however she is a naturally prominent horse who has been redistributed rearward on the map because there is no room for her in the positions she would prefer, meaning she is likely to race in an unfamiliar position — factor that into expectations.

runners_data.name: Shi Yang
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Good for Robson De Aguiar, so course conditions suit, but recent form reads 5417 and her trainer has 0 from 8 over the last 14 days; prominent style faces the same crowding problem at the front that afflicts several rivals here.

runners_data.name: Maire Rua
runners_data.note: Beautifully bred and unbeaten in two starts including a 7f win on Good for G M Lyons and Colin Keane — that jockey-trainer combination is formidable; she is a true prominent racer but has been mapped back because of pace congestion, and drawn 11 she may lack the room to assert her natural style early.

runners_data.name: Ibelieveicanfly
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes over for Aidan O'Brien on this OR 100 filly who has finished fourth three times in four runs, suggesting consistent ability without dominance; prominent style suits the shape and she is the most experienced horse in the field, though her tendency to be held up slightly makes her a target for the front half rather than the very lead.

runners_data.name: Snowing
runners_data.note: Two places from four runs, trained by A P O'Brien with Boudot in the saddle — that booking is notable; Good ground suits on the evidence and a 7f trip looks correct, but she has not won and faces a strong pace that will test her resolve in the final furlong.

runners_data.name: Blonde Over Blue
runners_data.note: OR 91 front-runner with a 7f win on Soft for Joseph O'Brien; she is a genuine leader who must assert from draw 8 against two rivals equally intent on the front, and her recent drop from 8f back to 7f suggests the trainer is looking for more pace — if she wins the duel she can be hard to peg back.

runners_data.name: Bellesque
runners_data.note: OR 91 with a win over 8f on Good and placed over 7f on Good, so stamina is not in doubt; another genuine leader for Joseph O'Brien stablemates in the same race creates interesting tactics, and she drops back from a mile — her front-running role could see her fade if the duel is truly fierce over the final furlong.

races.paceDynamic: Blonde Over Blue, Bellesque, and Lady Patrona all carry genuine front-running intentions and will contest the lead from the gates, guaranteeing a strong, searching gallop over Leopardstown's flat 7f on Good ground. With three horses fighting for the early positions, the pace will be honest to strong throughout, placing a premium on stamina and the ability to travel fluidly in a prominent position without expending unnecessary energy in the early exchanges. Timeless Tale, a confirmed prominent runner with a clean profile at this track and trip, is ideally suited to track the pace battle without being embroiled in it, arriving with energy to spend at the critical 2f pole. This race shape strongly favours resolute prominent racers who can settle just off a hot pace and produce a sustained late effort — hold-up types or pure closers are at a disadvantage given the honest gallop is unlikely to produce a true slow-burn collapse. The field also contains more naturally prominent horses than can realistically all secure their preferred slots: Maeda Matsu and Maire Rua are genuine prominent types redistributed rearward on the pace map, and Shi Yang also has prominent pretensions — among these, Maire Rua drawn widest and Maeda Matsu from a low draw are least likely to recover their natural position once three dedicated leaders seize the early fractions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong pace, prominent wins
scenarios.trigger: If Blonde Over Blue, Bellesque and Lady Patrona set a true strong gallop and the race is run end-to-end at an honest clip.
scenarios.body: The pace battle between the three leaders strings the field out from the first furlong, and the horse who travels smoothly just off the boil arrives with the freshest reserves at the 1f marker; this is the ideal setup for a well-rated prominent type who can quicken once the front-runners crack.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace duel, stamina test
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners genuinely battle for supremacy, creating an even faster early clip that turns the race into a stamina test from 3f out.
scenarios.body: With the pace exaggerated by a three-way duel, all prominent types are tested for resolution and the winner is likely the one with the best finishing attitude over this trip; horses with a pedigree or form pattern suggesting they get further than 7f have an edge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-runner lasts home
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three leaders gets a soft lead by breaking fastest and the others fail to press, allowing a solo front-runner to control fractions.
scenarios.body: A controlled early clip from a single leader means the pace is not truly punishing and stamina is less of a premium, enabling the front-runner to conserve enough energy to hold on under pressure; Blonde Over Blue with OR 91 and course experience is the most plausible beneficiary if she breaks cleanest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers pounce late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace war is exceptionally fierce and burns out all three leaders, creating a vacuum that mid-division horses can exploit in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Apollo's Comet and Maire Rua, though redistributed rearward on the map and not natural hold-up types, could benefit if the race falls apart in front; the caveat is that this scenario requires those horses to race genuinely out of their preferred role, which tempers confidence materially.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Blonde Over Blue, Bellesque or Lady Patrona win the early battle for the lead — if all three push hard from the gun, the pace could be extreme and the entire front three may tire, opening the door for Timeless Tale to cruise through.

Maire Rua with Colin Keane from draw 11 will need to push forward early to reclaim her natural prominent position — if traffic forces her to settle mid-pack, her chance is significantly compromised despite strong form credentials.

Maeda Matsu from draw 3 may attempt to burst forward early and mix it with the leaders despite the redistribution, creating an even more congested early pace scenario — Rory Cleary's tactics from the first furlong are worth monitoring closely.

Ibelieveicanfly's headgear flag (h) is noted — Ryan Moore may choose to drop her slightly to track the pace battle rather than be embroiled in it, which would be the tactically astute ride given three horses fighting up front.

Snowing's booking of Pierre-Charles Boudot for O'Brien suggests this filly is held in higher regard than her winless record implies — watch her market movement before the off as an indicator of stable confidence.

runners_data.name: Fort Vega
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up performer with solid course form at 7f on good going (four runs, three places), trained by Sheila Lavery; draw 11 is workable, but a 29-day break and a tendency to need things to fall right from rear means dependence on a strong gallop to generate the run-in.|

runners_data.name: Tokenomics
runners_data.note: Five-year-old prominent racer over 7-8f, David Marnane yard quiet at 0/16 in the past fortnight; steps back to 7f having run exclusively over 8f recently, and draw 9 gives a clean chance to secure prominent position if the redistribution frees up space.|

runners_data.name: Andab
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's three-year-old has strong placed form at 8f on good and runs in a visor; the drop to 7f is a query given all recent runs have been over a mile or more, and draw 20 will demand an early decision about how wide to travel.|

runners_data.name: Sindagan
runners_data.note: JP Murtagh's three-year-old won over this exact course and distance last time and placed twice before that at 7f on soft; draw 16 is the main concern — needs to travel wide or find an early gap — but the form at this trip is the most directly relevant in the race.|

runners_data.name: Dorset
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore confirmed front-runner for Aidan O'Brien, but the form string (8-9-4-9-7 over 7f on good) makes grim reading for a horse asked to set the pace; Moore's tactical intelligence is the saving grace, but this horse is here to make the race rather than win it on bare form.|

runners_data.name: Vafortino
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes's eight-year-old prominent racer has placed at 7f on good recently (third last time out); a well-travelled veteran who knows his job, but the age and the lack of a win from four recent similar-going starts tempers expectations.|

runners_data.name: Benevento
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who won over 8f on good 13 days ago and placed at 7f on good; Robson De Aguiar yard is quiet (0/8 past fortnight) but this horse is in form, and from draw 18 Egan will need to press hard early to cross and lead — feasible but it burns energy.|

runners_data.name: Temperance
runners_data.note: Kate McGivern's hold-up four-year-old wearing a hood; form figures of 7-7-11-6 on good suggest this level is a stretch, and with no win in the sample and only minor impact at similar going, this looks a difficult task in a 21-runner field.|

runners_data.name: Excellent Believe
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy aboard a prominent racer for Stephen Thorne, 70 days off the track; placed twice at 8f on good, but the step back to 7f and the layoff both require satisfactory evidence — draw 4 is good and Murphy's presence keeps interest alive.|

runners_data.name: Mirsky
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's seven-year-old prominent type with a win from nine good-ground attempts; the recent form (0-7-9-9-2) is patchy but the second at 8f on soft is recent, and Kieran Shoemark takes over — trip is a furlong short of his best distance.|

runners_data.name: Gleneagle Bay
runners_data.note: Colin Keane partners this hold-up six-year-old who won over 7f on good course and distance and wears a hood; draw 1 means rail position throughout, and his 5/9 record on good going is the best ground-form strike rate of the hold-up brigade — a key player in any late-closer scenario.|

runners_data.name: Rahmi
runners_data.note: Seamie Heffernan's seven-year-old hold-up type has won at 7f on good and placed at 8f on good twice in five recent runs; draw 21 is wide and his 2024 form has been inconsistent at this level, but he's a durable type who can arrive late if the pace holds.|

runners_data.name: Krasimir
runners_data.note: Strand Scorecard top selection, a natural prominent racer for Gordon Lyons pushed to a midfield position on the map due to overcrowding; form is consistently placed (four thirds and a win from six recent runs), and Reese Holohan's 7lb claim helps the bottom-weight cause — the key question is whether he can get closer to the pace than his mapped position suggests, which the Scorecard implies he can with low confidence.|

runners_data.name: Howd'yadoit
runners_data.note: Gary Carroll on a Lyons three-year-old who won over 5f on good but has now stepped up steadily in trip and class; all five recent efforts have been at 5-6f, so this 7f test is uncharted territory — the form suggests gate speed rather than staying power.|

runners_data.name: Oro Blanco
runners_data.note: Jessica Harrington's three-year-old has two wins on good going including over 7f, with a natural prominent style; pushed back on the map due to field congestion, draw 13 is neutral, and at OR 84 there is a handicap case if the run gets made — the style fit caveat (0.93) reminds that getting the position matters.|

runners_data.name: Victory Tip
runners_data.note: Henry de Bromhead's three-year-old is 86 days off the track after winning on heavy at the Curragh; the step up to 7f on good ground is new ground, draw 5 is fine, and Declan McDonogh takes over — the layoff and going change are the twin uncertainties.|

runners_data.name: Dark Viper
runners_data.note: Jessica Harrington's five-year-old wears a hood and has won over 9f on good ground, with natural prominent tendencies now mapped to midfield given field size; recent placed form (1-2-6 from last three on good) is solid, but 7f may be on the sharp side given a preference for more ground.|

runners_data.name: L L Koulsty
runners_data.note: Strand Scorecard danger, Rory Mulligan's 5lb claimer on a three-year-old who has won twice in the last five runs including at 7f on good going; draw 15 is manageable, John O'Donoghue's yard is active (1/5 fortnight), and the horse has finished placed in five of six recent starts — a strong profile for this race shape.|

runners_data.name: Collecting Coin
runners_data.note: W J Lee partners this four-year-old for Jennie Candlish who is a natural prominent racer; won over 8f on good and placed at 7f on soft, but the field congestion means he may find himself racing further back than ideal — draw 7 at least gives options going right.|

runners_data.name: Booyea
runners_data.note: Thomas Gibney's six-year-old hold-up type wearing a hood; placed at 8f on good and 8f on good before that, but 7f on good is untested and his draw of 6 gives some options to find a position. A 14-day turnaround keeps the yard's hand in but this is a difficult pitch.|

runners_data.name: Carnival Of Light
runners_data.note: Christophe Soumillon takes the ride on Charlie Johnston's four-year-old who won twice on standard artificial ground but has finished fourth both times on good turf; natural prominent style, pushed back by congestion, and the going switch to genuine turf good remains the outstanding question mark in his profile.|

races.paceDynamic: Dorset (draw 3, Ryan Moore) and Benevento (draw 18, David Egan) are the two confirmed front-runners and will contest the early lead, creating a genuine, honest gallop across 7 furlongs on good ground at Leopardstown — this is not a scenario where pace collapses. With 21 runners and a competitive handicap field, the fractions will be genuine from the jump, and the race is unlikely to set up for a dawdle-and-sprint. That honest pace on a flat track on good ground classically favours horses who can travel prominently just off the speed or produce a sustained late run from midfield — pure hold-up horses who need a stronger-than-honest gallop to generate sufficient gaps are at a slight disadvantage in a field where positions will be congested. This field holds more prominent-minded types than the pace map can accommodate: Krasimir, Collecting Coin, Carnival Of Light, Oro Blanco, and Dark Viper are all natural prominent racers who will find themselves shuffled back from their preferred position, with L L Koulsty and Tokenomics among those most likely to actually secure a berth on the pace; the tactical verdict is that horses able to settle just behind the front two and produce a sustained run in the straight — the prominent-to-midfield profile — are best served by this race shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Dorset and Benevento set a genuine gallop and a prominent racer travels smoothly just off them into the straight.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners maintain honest fractions and the prominent horses who secure a real position — L L Koulsty, Tokenomics, Sindagan — are best placed to pounce as the leaders tire in the final furlong. This shape is the dominant one given confirmed pace and good ground, rewarding those who can travel with cover and sustain their run.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Two Brave It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Dorset or Benevento — or both — show enough class to sustain their lead and the honest gallop fails to expose them.
scenarios.body: One of the confirmed front-runners dictates on their own terms once the other fades, converting pace-pressure into a winning advantage rather than a trap; Benevento's recent win over a similar trip and going makes this credible. Dorset with Moore's timing is the alternative, though the form string is less inspiring than Benevento's.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fierce enough to burn off the prominent racers and the genuine hold-up horses arrive with a late rattle down the stands rail.
scenarios.body: Gleneagle Bay, Fort Vega, and Rahmi have the profiles to benefit if the early fractions are truly punishing, arriving fresh into a tired field. Gleneagle Bay in particular has course and distance form and a low draw to maximise ground saved.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos, Upset
scenarios.trigger: If the congested midfield breaks in favour of a displaced prominent type who secures better ground than expected and the pace collapses slightly.
scenarios.body: Krasimir or Collecting Coin, natural prominent racers pushed to midfield, could outrun their mapped position if the race compresses and gaps appear earlier than expected; Krasimir's consistent placed form (four places from six recent runs) keeps the Strand Scorecard top selection relevant here despite the positional compromise. Carnival Of Light is the wildcard, having won twice on standard ground though Leopardstown good is a different test.

watchPoints.text: Dorset and Benevento will contest the early lead vigorously — watch for Benevento from draw 18 burning significant energy crossing the field to assert, which could compromise his stamina in the final furlong.

L L Koulsty (draw 15) needs Rory Mulligan to find a clear run from a wide draw in a 21-runner field — if he gets shuffled wide or checked entering the straight, his chance is compromised despite strong form credentials.

Krasimir is the Scorecard selection but is mapped to midfield due to natural prominent runners crowding the early positions — watch whether Reese Holohan angles forward early to get closer to his true racing position, as this determines whether the selection delivers.

runners_data.name: Nola Soul
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard selection: a three-time winner at 7f on Good ground who steps up to 1m1f in a race where the strong pace suits a prominent runner — Seamie Heffernan from stall 1 can dictate her position just off the lead throughout without expending unnecessary energy; sim-going record of 3/3 on Good is a significant positive.

runners_data.name: Green Dreamer
runners_data.note: A confirmed front-runner whose rider Sheridan will look to press forward from stall 5, though five rivals with identical lead intent means Sheridan faces a battle just to secure the rail and an honest pace could undermine Green Dreamer's chance of lasting home at 1m1f.

runners_data.name: Aix La Chapelle
runners_data.note: Soumillon partners a two-year-old whose sole win came over 7f at Leopardstown on Good ground, so the step to 1m1f is unproven; listed as hold-up here only because the field is overloaded with front-runners — in reality this is a prominent-racing type, and its shown position should be treated with a style-fit discount of 0.80.

runners_data.name: Jesus Green
runners_data.note: Limited form — a single second-place finish over 8f on Good — means there is genuine uncertainty about both class and stamina here; Colin Keane is one of the most effective jockeys in Ireland but has very little form to work with and the horse is an unknown quantity stepping up in grade significantly.

runners_data.name: Pikachu
runners_data.note: The most experienced runner in the field with five starts, and a recent win over 8f on Soft suggests stamina is not an issue at 1m1f; Good-going form is mixed (0W from two prominent rides on Good) but the OR of 106 is the highest in the race and Charlie Johnston's yard has been in fair form.

runners_data.name: Victory Speech
runners_data.note: Won on Good ground over 8f at Leopardstown last time — directly relevant course-and-distance form — and Gavin Ryan will look to deploy this horse's natural front-running style; with five pace rivals in opposition, Victory Speech may be crowded out early from stall 7, and the wide draw adds an energy cost in a race where early position is fiercely contested.

runners_data.name: Quest For Stars
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in three starts, all on Good ground, and Charlie Appleby's yard is firing with a T14 strike rate of 6/17; James Doyle is an intelligent front-running jockey and stall 8 gives the option to either press forward or slot in just behind if the pace turns manic — the strongest credentials among the front-running group.

runners_data.name: Darkness Falls
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore partners this A P O'Brien runner who won on Good over 8f just 14 days ago — the freshest recent winning form in the field; Moore will likely be patient enough to avoid the early pace battle, but the horse's natural front-running style means it may be dragged into the speed argument regardless of intention.

runners_data.name: Shakespeare
runners_data.note: Stepped up to win over 7f Good last time and the Boudot-O'Brien combination is classy, though three starts have been over 7f maximum and the extra distance here is the key unknown; from stall 3 there is every chance of being sucked into the early pace war alongside four rivals with the same instinct to lead.

runners_data.name: Zarak Pasha
runners_data.note: Won over 9f on Good ground most recently, which makes Zarak Pasha the only runner in the field with a victory beyond 8f, and that stamina edge could prove crucial if the strong pace tests the others; Declan McDonogh from stall 2 can sit behind Nola Soul and the front-runners and produce a sustained run if the pace genuinely hotpots.

races.paceDynamic: Five horses carry genuine front-running or prominent intent into this 1m1f contest — Green Dreamer, Quest For Stars, Victory Speech, Darkness Falls, and Shakespeare will all want to press forward from the gates, guaranteeing a strong early tempo on Good ground at Leopardstown. The prominent contingent of Nola Soul, Pikachu, Zarak Pasha, and Jesus Green will be forced to race just off a fierce pace rather than enjoying the comfort of a soft lead, creating a compressed mid-race dynamic with traffic danger almost certain 2-3 out as the field turns for home. Crucially, Aix La Chapelle is flagged as redistributed — a natural prominent runner shown at hold-up due to the field's lack of genuine closers, meaning this race has even more pace pressure baked in than it appears on paper, and the one runner supposedly "closing" is not a true hold-up type. This shape emphatically favours the horse with the best combination of tactical speed to hold a prime position just off the contested lead and the stamina to sustain that effort through the final two furlongs — a strong-travelling prominent racer with proven Good-ground form is the profile this pace scenario rewards most handsomely.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the strong pace burns off the contested front-runners from 3f out, leaving a well-positioned prominent racer to stride clear in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The five front-runners fight among themselves for early supremacy, setting a genuine gallop that stretches the field, and a horse sitting a length or two off the pace arrives with a sustained run to collar the tiring leaders at the line; Nola Soul's proven 7f Good-ground form translates to this 1m1f on a testing pace and she is ideally placed from stall 1 to control a prime tracking position throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Breaks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one of the leading quartet asserts enough authority early to control the tempo and steal a decisive advantage from the top of the straight.
scenarios.body: Quest For Stars's unbeaten three-from-three record on Good ground and James Doyle's ability to dictate from stall 8 allow the Appleby runner to roll to the front and set only a fair pace, conserving enough energy to quicken when asked; a race run at a controlled rather than suicidal gallop would expose the field's lack of a genuine sitting closer and reward the horse best able to dominate from the front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Helps Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the early speed fractures by halfway and a horse tracking in mid-division finds an unimpeded run down the centre.
scenarios.body: Pikachu's recent winning form at 8f shows improvement at this trip and David Egan could steal a march by sitting sixth or seventh as the pace implodes ahead; the open field and Good ground allow a horse with a strong finishing kick to pick off tired rivals in the final furlong, provided traffic clears early enough in the straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so severe that all prominent horses wilt and a genuine hold-up run produces a late rattle.
scenarios.body: This scenario is materially discounted because Aix La Chapelle, the only runner mapped to a rear position, is a redistributed prominent type rather than a natural closer, meaning the profile required to exploit this shape has no genuine representative in the field; even if the pace is brutal, the lack of a true hold-up horse means no runner is in position to deliver a sustained late challenge from off the bridle from the back.

watchPoints.text: Quest For Stars (stall 8) and Green Dreamer (stall 5) will both attempt to lead — watch the first two furlongs for a battle for the rail that could inject an unsustainably fierce pace and compromise both their finishing efforts.

Nola Soul from stall 1 sits in the perfect stalking position but the prominent congestion means Seamie Heffernan must be alert to a wall of horses attempting to cut across and take her ground between 2f and 3f out.

Aix La Chapelle is mapped to hold-up but is a natural prominent type — if Soumillon elects to race forward in keeping with the horse's style, the field has even more pace pressure than the drawn positions suggest, further compressing the prominent group and increasing traffic risk.

Darkness Falls ran just 14 days ago and Ryan Moore may attempt to settle the horse off the pace; if the fractions are fast enough to compromise its stamina, watch for it to fade tamely inside the final furlong despite carrying winning fitness.

Zarak Pasha is the only runner proven at beyond 8f, having won at 9f — if the strong pace turns this into a genuine stamina test, McDonogh from stall 2 is ideally positioned to deliver a late challenge that catches out rivals flattening out.

runners_data.name: Purview
runners_data.note: Top-rated hold-up performer for Dermot Weld and Colin Keane; three wins from three starts on Good ground and a sparkling recent form string of 251-11 make this the class horse in the race, perfectly set up by a contested pace to deliver her trademark sustained late burst.

runners_data.name: Green Impact
runners_data.note: Shane Foley's mount wants to lead or race very prominently; two wins at 12f on Good give her some credentials, but she faces a fierce battle for position from the outset against Arabian Crown and Thread Of Gold, and her recent form has tailed off in running — placed just once in her last three.

runners_data.name: Sons And Lovers
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy rides this consistent JP O'Brien-trained five-year-old who races prominently; hasn't won since finishing third at 12f on Good but has filled the places reliably, and the step up to 1m4f on Good suits a horse that stays well and travels economically off the pace.

runners_data.name: Gaucher
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins sends out this seven-year-old with David Egan aboard; best form has come on Soft or Standard ground rather than Good, which is a mild concern, but the horse has tactical speed from a prominent position and a win at 10f on Good ground suggests he is not without a chance if conditions are kinder than expected.

runners_data.name: Arabian Crown
runners_data.note: James Doyle's Charlie Appleby runner has the widest lead-style profile and draws widest among the front-runners in stall 1; his record shows one place from two runs on Good, and he will burn energy asserting his lead against multiple rivals, making it hard to see him lasting home against stronger closers.

runners_data.name: Piazza San Marco
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore partners this lightly raced three-year-old for Aidan O'Brien; has shown ability at this trip on Good ground in finishing third at 14f, but a modest OR of 102 puts him at a disadvantage against the older horses, and he will need to be on the pace from stall 4 to make his presence felt.

runners_data.name: James J Braddock
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard's headline selection; JP O'Brien's lightly weighted three-year-old sits mid-division and has winning form on Good ground at 10f, with a 76-day absence for a yard firing at 6/56 in the past fortnight — the horse will need a truly strong pace to unlock his late gallop, which this race is set to provide.

runners_data.name: In My Teens
runners_data.note: Gary Carroll's hold-up performer for Gavin Cromwell wears headgear and has shown a tendency to find trouble in running; a win at 12f on Good is encouraging but three recent placeless efforts at this track on Good, including a heavy defeat last time, make it hard to build a case at OR 109.

runners_data.name: Goodie Two Shoes
runners_data.note: Declan McDonogh rides this JP O'Brien seven-year-old who wears a tongue tie; won over 14f on Good and was second at the same trip, so the distance and going suit, and a mid-division style means he is ideally placed to benefit from a genuine pace — a live each-way threat in this scenario.

runners_data.name: Asakir
runners_data.note: Ben Coen takes the ride on JP Murtagh's three-year-old who races prominently from stall 6; the horse finished seventh on his 14f Good debut which is a concern, though his second at 13f and a win at 10f suggest he has ability — OR 100 is the lowest in the field and he will need to improve sharply.

runners_data.name: Thread Of Gold
runners_data.note: WJ Lee partners this Willie Mullins three-year-old who has won twice recently, most recently at 12f on Soft; the step up to 1m4f on Good is an unknown and she will likely race prominently, but facing seasoned older horses in a Group 3 off an OR of 104 represents a significant class test.

races.paceDynamic: Arabian Crown, Green Impact, Thread Of Gold and Piazza San Marco all want to race prominently or lead, guaranteeing a contested, honest gallop over this 1m4f trip on Good ground at Leopardstown. Arabian Crown (draw 1) and Thread Of Gold (draw 5) are the most likely to press for the early lead, with Green Impact and Piazza San Marco applying further pressure from the front half of the field, ensuring the pace is genuine rather than dawdled. With four runners competing for the early positions, no single horse will be able to control the race cheaply, which means the strong tempo will stretch the field and expose any stamina limitations in the front rank. This shape emphatically favours hold-up and mid-division horses who can conserve energy early, track the pace from off it and deploy a sustained late run — making Purview, James J Braddock and Goodie Two Shoes the profiles best placed to capitalise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Closers Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the contested pace from Arabian Crown, Green Impact, Thread Of Gold and Piazza San Marco burns along honestly, draining the front rank entering the straight.
scenarios.body: The mid-division and hold-up horses are gifted a pace to chase on Good ground, allowing them to pick off the tiring leaders in the final two furlongs; Purview's proven ability to deliver a sustained late run and James J Braddock's strong finishing profile make them the primary beneficiaries of this classic honest-pace meltdown.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Battle Collapses
scenarios.trigger: If Arabian Crown or Thread Of Gold seizes an uncontested lead after the initial scrapping resolves and a false pace results in a muddling gallop.
scenarios.body: One pacemaker dominates once rivals are outpaced early and the race becomes a sprint home from a slow tempo, favouring those with enough tactical speed to sit close to the leader; Sons And Lovers and Gaucher, both prominent-style runners with quick finishes, benefit from a compact field that makes a late swooping run harder to execute.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the genuine pace is consistently strong but one prominent horse conserves energy by tracking just behind the leaders rather than leading, and times the challenge to perfection.
scenarios.body: Gaucher or Sons And Lovers, anchored just off the pace at a strong gallop, finds the leaders spent enough to hold off the closers in a race where the winning position is two lengths off the front; the Good ground and honest tempo reward the horse that travels best rather than the horse that runs fastest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Gate Crashes
scenarios.trigger: If the genuine pace is so severe that it brings the entire field into contention late and a lightly weighted or improving runner exploits the chaos.
scenarios.body: Thread Of Gold or Piazza San Marco, both carrying a lower weight burden in a field that has burned itself out, finds a wall of tiring horses to pick through and is gifted an opening; this is a low-probability shape because it requires multiple factors to align simultaneously and the form of the leading fancies is superior.

watchPoints.text: Purview vs James J Braddock — the Strand Scorecard's top and danger are both hold-up horses entirely dependent on the pace holding up; if the four front-runners fail to collectively maintain a genuine gallop all the way to the straight, neither will have enough to pass leaders with petrol still in the tank.

Arabian Crown (stall 1) vs Thread Of Gold (stall 5) vs Green Impact (stall 8) — watch the first furlong closely as three lead-style horses fight for the front position; whichever horse loses that battle will be forced to race at an uncomfortable, energy-sapping pace in the early stages.

Green Impact's place in the market — she is effectively a lead-or-nothing runner whose recent form figures (4-4-2) have all come racing prominently, and if she cannot secure a clear lead she may be shuffled back and compromise her race entirely.

Goodie Two Shoes at 14f on Good — the JP O'Brien seven-year-old has won and placed at this exact trip on this going, meaning he is quietly well-suited and could outrun a bigger price if James J Braddock underperforms or gets blocked in traffic.

In My Teens — headgear and a history of finding trouble in running; Gary Carroll will need to find clear passage turning for home in an 11-runner field, and any check in momentum will be fatal to a horse that already showed fragile recent form.

runners_data.name: Precise
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore partners a horse with an exceptional record on similar ground (6/6 Good-ground runs, four wins), held-up tactics suit perfectly in a hot-pace race, and recent form (2-1-1-1) over this exact trip makes her a chief danger.

runners_data.name: Blue Bolt
runners_data.note: Colin Keane's mount arrives as the highest-rated runner (OR 119) with four consecutive wins including at Group level, consistently prominent on Good ground over a mile, and the wide draw (9) should not inconvenience her on a flat course where Keane can dictate his own terms.

runners_data.name: City Of Memphis
runners_data.note: An unbeaten front-runner this season but returning from 111 days off is a meaningful concern; W J Lee will need to balance controlling the pace against the fitness deficit, and her record on soft (1/7f/SOF) means today's Good ground is preferred ground.

runners_data.name: Fallen Angel
runners_data.note: A natural front-runner equipped with headgear, she has beaten the best over this mile before, but recent form (110-43) shows a loss of her earlier dominance and she faces fierce early competition for the lead from two other confirmed pace-setters; this contested scenario is the chief risk to her chances.

runners_data.name: Carolina Jetstream
runners_data.note: Her recent record (0W2P in four Good-ground runs, form string 402682) exposes a horse who may briefly fight for position without being able to sustain it; a trainer with 0/8 in the 14-day window and 22 days since last run add limited confidence she can trouble the principals.

runners_data.name: Duckadilly
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse with two Good-turf wins at this trip, returning from 55 days off for a small yard (T14: 1/20), and a sim-going record of 7/8 showing inconsistency; Ben Coen will look to emerge late but the class step to Group 1 level is a steep ask.

runners_data.name: Pivotal Attack
runners_data.note: A three-year-old prominent runner with only one win from five recent Good-ground attempts (0W1P in that sample), taking a significant class leap into Group 1 company; Oisin Murphy's presence is the main asset but form figures (-38418) give little encouragement here.

runners_data.name: Meriden
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's three-year-old has an impressive form sequence (111126) and four wins from Good/Soft turf, but a sim-going record of 6/11 shows inconsistency, J M Sheridan rides a horse taking a dramatic class hike, and the 6th on latest run was her first blemish at the mile trip.

races.paceDynamic: Fallen Angel, City Of Memphis, and Carolina Jetstream all want to lead, creating a near-certainty of a contested, high-tempo gallop from the outset over Leopardstown's flat mile on Good ground. City Of Memphis has been dominant in her front-running role this season but returns from 111 days off, while Fallen Angel has the headgear and the Group 1 class to fight hard for the early rail, meaning the pace battle itself may begin before the first bend. Carolina Jetstream's recent form (402682) suggests she is unlikely to sustain a meaningful challenge but will nonetheless contribute to a genuinely strong early fraction. This race shape overwhelmingly favours prominent and hold-up horses who can conserve energy through the early stages and deploy a sustained late run — in particular those with the class to pick up efficiently once the pace collapses in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hot Pace, Closers Reign
scenarios.trigger: If the three-way duel for the lead burns out the front-runners inside the final quarter-mile, leaving the race open for those tracking or held up.
scenarios.body: Fallen Angel, City Of Memphis, and Carolina Jetstream sustain a fierce gallop that strips the leaders of reserves past the two-furlong marker, allowing prominent and hold-up runners with superior class to sweep through. Blue Bolt, tracking keenly with Colin Keane from a wide draw, and Precise, patient under Ryan Moore, are the primary beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Blue Bolt Stalks and Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Blue Bolt travels comfortably just off the hot pace and quickens decisively in the straight as the leaders tie up.
scenarios.body: Keane positions Blue Bolt in the slipstream of the early leaders from draw 9, and once the tempo subsides Blue Bolt's superior OR of 119 and unblemished recent form (1-1111) allows her to accelerate clear. The top-rated runner in the field, she has won four consecutive times on Good turf over this trip and represents the profile this race shape is built to reward.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives Carnage
scenarios.trigger: If City Of Memphis or Fallen Angel steals a march, the pace war between the other two leaders neutralises each other, and one front-runner is left in front going into the straight.
scenarios.body: City Of Memphis, returning from a lengthy 111-day absence but unbeaten in three this season, has the class and natural aptitude to dictate if Fallen Angel and Carolina Jetstream contest each other's position and fade; Fallen Angel, equipped with headgear and dropping back to a mile she has won at, is the alternative beneficiary if she secures a clean lead.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Held-Up Finisher Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is even more extreme than anticipated and the race becomes a sprint finish with runners widest and deepest coming off the bend.
scenarios.body: Precise or Meriden, both operating from hold-up positions and both with strong recent form figures on Good turf, could emerge from the pack if every horse in front weakens simultaneously. Precise's six-from-six record on similar going and Meriden's impressive winning streak make them the ones to benefit, though their reliance on an extreme meltdown limits this scenario's probability.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Fallen Angel or City Of Memphis secures the early rail; if both are scrubbing along to lead before the half-mile, the fractions could be extreme enough to compromise both and fundamentally reshape the finish.

Blue Bolt's wide draw (9) requires Keane to either push forward early or settle wider than ideal — if the early pace drags her into contention sooner than planned, her stamina reserves entering the straight could be tested.
City Of Memphis is 111 days off the track; watch for any signs of greenness or lack of peak fitness in the paddock and early stages — if she is not wound up, the whole pace dynamic changes.

Precise under Ryan Moore could be entirely overlooked in the market given the noise around the front-runners; Moore will likely find a position just off the pace from the inside draw (1), which is a patient hold-up pattern perfectly suited to this race shape.

Fallen Angel's headgear (hg:p — presumably a hood or cheekpieces) is a detail to track at the start — if it has a calming effect and she settles rather than battles, she becomes a more potent threat to last home than her recent form (110-43) suggests.

runners_data.name: Hazdann
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on Good last time and holds solid course form; Hayes-Weld combination is reliable, and the hold-up style suits a genuinely-run mile — only concern is whether he gets a clear run through what will be a congested midfield coming off the final bend.

runners_data.name: Cowardofthecounty
runners_data.note: Consistent record shows two wins and three places from seven runs on Good, and the Joseph O'Brien yard has been active; however, this horse's natural instinct is to race at the back of the field — squeezed to midfield on the pace map because the race shape is loaded with hold-up types, meaning he may not get the ground-saver position he truly needs.

runners_data.name: Charles Fort
runners_data.note: Front-runner who should be involved in a direct duel with Faiyum from the off; Soumillon is a canny rider capable of conserving energy even when pressed, and his stall 1 position is ideal to slot straight into the lead rail without being forced wide — last two runs on Good show he can handle the ground.

runners_data.name: Princess Child
runners_data.note: Five-year-old mare in poor recent form with three consecutive finishes outside the frame; Joseph O'Brien yard is busy but her last six runs include four double-figure finishes, and she does not carry enough quality at OR 100 to threaten at Group 2 level on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Isaac Newton
runners_data.note: The standout form horse in the field at OR 110 with recent wins over 8f and 9f on Good going, and Ryan Moore from the outside draw in stall 10 can plot a clean rails-less route; his hold-up style is tailor-made for a truly-run race, and six of his last six runs have come on Good ground so no going concerns.

runners_data.name: Quddwah
runners_data.note: Highest-rated runner at OR 114 but hasn't run since December and carries a noted tendency to fade in the finish; returning from 168 days off is a significant unknown, and James Doyle will need to find the sweet spot between the two front-runners — his sole Good-ground run this year saw him finish 15th over 8f, which tempers confidence.

runners_data.name: Power Blue
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard's top-rated selection; David Egan's booking is positive and the horse's last win came over 7f on Good going — stepping up to 1m is within range for a prominent runner, and if Egan can slot him just off the speed battle behind Faiyum and Charles Fort he avoids the midfield scrum entirely.

runners_data.name: Faiyum
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who will be busiest in the early stages contesting the lead with Charles Fort; Colin Keane is an astute tactician who will decide quickly whether to force the pace or let Charles Fort go, and his record shows a win and a place in his last two Good-ground starts — if Charles Fort blinks, Faiyum takes over and is dangerous.

runners_data.name: Audience
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with excellent recent consistency, finishing second or third in three of his last six on Good going, and W.J. Lee knows this horse well; prominent style suits a competitive gallop and he should track the speed without burning petrol early — the flat Leopardstown mile suits his profile but he needs a clear run at the two-furlong pole.

runners_data.name: Expanded
runners_data.note: Consistent placed record with two second-place finishes in his last two runs, trained by Aidan O'Brien and ridden by Boudot, but returning from 118 days off is a notable query; drawn wide in stall 9, he is likely to be pushed slightly further back than his natural prominent style would dictate given the pace congestion ahead of him.

races.paceDynamic: Faiyum and Charles Fort are confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off on this flat Leopardstown mile, creating an honest, competitive gallop rather than a falsely-run affair. With four runners wanting prominent positions — Quddwah, Power Blue, Audience, and Expanded all chasing the same ground — there will be significant congestion in the first half-mile, compressing the field and creating traffic danger two to three furlongs out. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate cleanly; Faiyum, drawn widest of the two leaders in stall 2, is most likely to dominate on the front end, while Charles Fort from stall 1 should track him, but both Quddwah and Audience are most likely to slot into the prominent positions behind them given class and jockey quality, leaving Power Blue and Expanded slightly further back than ideal. A genuinely-run pace on Good ground over a flat mile at Leopardstown historically suits hold-up horses who can finish strongly through a tiring pack, giving the edge to those with a confirmed strong late run — but Isaac Newton and Hazdann must find a way past the midfield congestion to capitalise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Gallop, Closers Deliver
scenarios.trigger: If Faiyum and Charles Fort set a genuine honest pace that strings the field out and clears the way for strong finishers from off the pace.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners burn each other up through a competitive gallop, leaving the race to those held up or tracking in the last two furlongs as the pace collapses late; Good ground on a flat track gives no hiding place for those who have burned petrol early. Hold-up horses with the strongest finishing kicks — Isaac Newton and Hazdann — find their optimal conditions here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fierce enough to destroy the hold-up horses' finishing kick but one prominent tracker conserves energy and pounces late from the chasing pack.
scenarios.body: Power Blue, sitting just behind the battle and avoiding the worst of the early fractions, finds a clear run from the two-furlong pole and picks off rivals as the true pace-setters tire; this suits a horse with his profile — prominent without being drawn into the speed battle, able to quicken on a flat track. Quddwah carries the fade-in-finish flag, so Power Blue is the most credible prominent beneficiary if the shape sets up this way.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outkicks Field
scenarios.trigger: If Charles Fort or Faiyum wins the early duel, settles in front at a sustainable clip, and proves impossible to reel in on a flat, easy-galloping track.
scenarios.body: Should the contested early stages not result in a true burn-up but instead one leader pinching a lead at a controlled tempo from two furlongs out, the prominent horses never get close enough to challenge and closers run out of track; Charles Fort, ridden by Soumillon who can save a horse's energy from the front, is the more likely beneficiary given his draw in stall 1. Faiyum also profiles as a winner here given his front-running form.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Wide-Draw Late
scenarios.trigger: If chaotic early exchanges cause a pace collapse mid-race, favouring a hold-up horse drawn widest who avoids all trouble.
scenarios.body: Isaac Newton from stall 10 avoids the early congestion entirely and Ryan Moore can plot a clean outside path to the two-furlong pole; Hazdann from stall 7 similarly has enough daylight to come late but the flat track and likely genuine pace makes a true late lunge harder to execute without a strong pace having been truly run. Both must time their runs perfectly to pounce.

watchPoints.text: Isaac Newton and Hazdann are both hold-up horses navigating a congested midfield — watch for traffic trouble between the two-furlong and one-furlong poles where the prominent pack could block both horses simultaneously.

Faiyum and Charles Fort will contest the lead from the off — if either refuses to give ground the pace will be genuinely fierce and could compromise every horse within two lengths of the front in the final furlong.

Quddwah's 168-day absence and noted fade-in-finish flag makes him a significant risk if he hits the front too early; James Doyle must judge the tempo precisely or he bleeds out in the final furlong under full Group 2 pressure.

Power Blue is the Scorecard's top selection but his trainer T14 figure shows zero winners from eight — watch whether David Egan can compensate with a bold prominent position to offset any stable wobble in form.

Cowardofthecounty's redistribution to midfield on the map understates the fact that he is a true hold-up horse — if he finds himself hemmed in behind the prominent pack rather than in the clear air at the rear, his race may be effectively over before straightening for home.

runners_data.name: Almaqam

runners_data.note: Shane Foley's mount carries headgear (p) and has not run for 48 days, which adds a fitness question mark; has shown pace in previous starts but a maximum of OR 116 and no wins in three runs on good ground suggests this is a horse more likely to set the tempo than finish in front of it.

runners_data.name: Lambourn
runners_data.note: Declan McDonogh's mount hasn't run for 49 days and has mixed form at 12f on soft and good — dropping back to 1m2f from a 1m4f campaign makes sense, but OR 119 and patchy recent form means he needs a truly extreme test of stamina to get involved.

runners_data.name: A Boy Named Susie
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien's three-year-old is unbeaten on good ground across five runs (1W4P) and Oisin Murphy takes over in a clear positive booking — a natural prominent racer drawn in stall 2, which should let Murphy tuck in behind the pace early and produce a sustained challenge from two furlongs out; the Strand Scorecard identifies this as the key danger to Item.

runners_data.name: Hawk Mountain
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien's second string alongside Constitution River — a front-runner by inclination but one who was beaten into sixth at 10f on good ground last time, and with only 0W from 1 start on similar going at this trip, his role is likely to contribute to the pace rather than win the race.

races.paceDynamic: Item, Hotazhell, and Hawk Mountain all want to be on or near the lead, guaranteeing a strong early gallop over Leopardstown's flat 1m2f on good ground — this is not a race where anyone stumbles into a falsely run contest. Item (Colin Keane) is the class act of the front-runners and will likely dictate terms from draw 4, with Hotazhell pressing from the inside rail and Hawk Mountain applying further pressure from draw 5, meaning the pace will be honest and sustained throughout. That relentless tempo will stretch the field and ensure stamina becomes the defining quality in the closing stages, favouring horses who can travel with cover and deliver a sustained finishing effort rather than a sharp sprint. The field also holds more prominent types than can all secure their ideal position — Constitution River (Ryan Moore, draw 3) and A Boy Named Susie (Oisin Murphy, draw 2) both want to be prominent, and with three genuine front-runners ahead of them, at least one will be forced to race slightly wider or deeper than preferred; Item is the one most likely to dictate uncontested, and this race shape strongly favours prominent-to-midfield closers who can track a true pace and sustain their run through the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace, Stamina Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Item controls from the front and the three-way early battle between Item, Hotazhell, and Hawk Mountain sets a truly searching gallop, the race becomes a test of staying power at Group 1 level.
scenarios.body: Item's rivals battle for supremacy up front and burn themselves out, allowing a horse with superior stamina and cruising speed to pick them off — a horse travelling kindly in second or third who quickens clear from two furlongs out wins.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Item Dictates and Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Item (Colin Keane) gets a soft lead and is able to control the pace without being seriously pressured early, switching off beautifully before quickening again.
scenarios.body: Item's top Racing Post Rating, consistent form on good ground, and ability to control his own tempo make him capable of front-running success if rivals don't push hard enough in the early stages — his 4W record from 4 starts on similar going underlines his suitability.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Mop Up Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front-running trio genuinely burn each other out and the pace collapses in the final two furlongs, horses coming from midfield who have been able to conserve energy could sweep past.
scenarios.body: Almaqam, who has shown the ability to finish off strongly from midfield on good ground, is the natural beneficiary of a truly run race that turns into a stamina test for the whole field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If the pace scenario muddles slightly and a prominent racer sits just off the leaders without being dragged into the early battle, that horse could pinch a lead at the top of the straight and hold on.
scenarios.body: Constitution River (Ryan Moore) is ideally drawn in stall 3 to slot into a prominent position without having to fight for it, and if the front-runners cancel each other out, Ryan Moore's tactical intelligence from that draw could be decisive.

watchPoints.text: A Boy Named Susie (draw 2, Oisin Murphy) will look to track Item and Constitution River from a position just off the pace — watch whether Murphy can slot in quietly or is forced wide early by the crowded prominent group.

Hotazhell (draw 1, headgear, 48 days off) could cut out an unsustainably fast early pace if Shane Foley sends him forward aggressively from the inside rail — a very fast opening quarter will accelerate the stamina test significantly.

Hawk Mountain (draw 5) is likely to be shuffled back after the initial battle for position with Item and Hotazhell — watch whether Boudot elects to drop him in or fights for prominence, as that early decision will define how much petrol he has at the finish.

Constitution River (Ryan Moore, draw 3) has won twice at 10f on good ground but has never faced a pace this strong at Group 1 level — watch whether Moore is able to park him just behind the battle or is drawn into chasing the tempo earlier than ideal.

Lambourn (49 days off, dropping back from 1m4f) — if the pace does collapse or the race comes to a stamina-sapping crawl in the straight, Declan McDonogh's patient ride from midfield could give him a late opportunity, but he needs the extreme end of the stamina scenario to be live.

runners_data.name: Evanesco
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Charlie Johnston and David Egan; has Good-ground form and won his last start over 12f, stepping up markedly in trip here — if he gets into a war with Madbadanddangerous and Minella Rockett from flag-fall, his stamina over 1m5f is an open question.

runners_data.name: Wyman
runners_data.note: Progressive three-year-old for Mrs Harrington with Shane Foley aboard; two wins in last four including at 13f on Good, and if he can slot into a genuine prominent position behind the pace war, his profile suits a strong-gallop test.

runners_data.name: Counting Coup

runners_data.name: Comfort Zone

runners_data.name: Cannes

runners_data.name: Poetic Sound

runners_data.name: Westminster Moon

runners_data.name: Yousaynothingatall

runners_data.name: Truth Be Told

runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up type who ran just 5 days ago — that rapid turnaround is the defining factor; placed at 16f Good in 2024 but recent form reads 0-9-0 and the quick reappearance suggests connections are hunting a specific target rather than expecting a peak run.

runners_data.name: Glenroyal
runners_data.note: Four-year-old O'Brien with Chris Hayes; won at 10f and 13f Good but recent efforts at 17-20f have been very poor, and the return to a more suitable 1m5f could see a bounce-back, though the yard's roster in this race creates internal competition for tactics.

races.paceDynamic: Evanesco, Madbadanddangerous, and Minella Rockett are all confirmed front-runners who will contest the early lead hard in a 26-runner field over 1m5f on Good ground, making a strong, sustained gallop virtually certain from the outset. That relentless early tempo over this stamina-testing trip will stretch the field significantly, burning off rivals who lack the resolution to see out the distance under pressure. The race is likely to be won by a horse who can sit just off the boiling pace in a genuine prominent position or track from mid-division with a powerful staying finish — pure hold-up horses will have too much ground to make up if the pace is honest throughout. This field contains far more prominent types than can realistically secure that position: Factual Fact, Star Harbour, Night Moon, Diamond Exchange, Sunny South West, and Immutable are all natural prominent racers who are likely to find themselves shuffled back into midfield, with Cannes (Colin Keane), Wyman, Port Of Spain, and Yousaynothingatall most likely to actually command the prominent berths given quality of pilot and yard.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong pace, stayer prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners set a fierce gallop that decimates the field, leaving a true stayer to reel them in off a strong pace.
scenarios.body: The relentless early fractions will punish any horse without genuine stamina at 1m5f on Good ground, turning this into a thorough test of resolution. A prominent tracker with proven stamina who can quicken off a strong tempo is ideally placed, as the pace-setters will have done the damage well before the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace collapse, prominent striker
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three front-runners gains a decisive advantage and the pace becomes uneven, allowing a well-placed prominent type to strike at a critical moment.
scenarios.body: Evanesco in particular has won on Good ground and could dictate if the others fade, creating a scenario where a horse in a close-tracking prominent position can land a decisive blow without overextending.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up horse swoops late
scenarios.trigger: If the strong early gallop is truly sustained and the field strings out, creating enough space for a genuine closer to pick up the pieces in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Comfort Zone won over 17f on Good and is a legitimate hold-up type; This Songisforyou placed over 12f on Good and is trained for these tests. Both will need the pace scenario to play perfectly and plenty of room in a 26-runner field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace implodes, chaos reigns
scenarios.trigger: If two or more front-runners clash and burn out early, causing the pace to collapse and creating an unpredictable scramble for the lead with the field bunching.
scenarios.body: In a 26-runner field at 1m5f, a collapse in the pace would benefit horses that can switch tactical gears, though this remains unlikely given the confirmed aggressive profiles of all three pace-setters. Night Moon and Factual Fact, natural prominent types pushed back, could find themselves in an unexpectedly good position if the field concertinas mid-race.

watchPoints.text: Evanesco (draw 12), Madbadanddangerous (draw 20), and Minella Rockett (draw 26) will battle hard from the gates — watch which of the three establishes the lead earliest, as the one who settles quickest will last longest and dictate how punishing the early fractions become.

Cannes and Truth Be Told are the two horses most likely to dictate the outcome if they can sit prominently just off the pace war — watch how quickly Colin Keane positions Cannes in the first quarter-mile, as a wide early draw (16) in a 26-runner field risks getting caught wide or losing position.

Star Harbour (draw 2) has an inside berth that gives him the best chance of any of the redistributed prominent types to actually hold a forward position — if he does get cover on the rail and the inside, his place claims improve significantly.

Yousaynothingatall with Oisin Murphy from draw 21 is a notable jockey-booking angle: Murphy does not take ordinary handicap rides without purpose, and if he can track the pace from a handy position this three-year-old's consistent form makes him a live threat to the principals.

runners_data.name: Aviatrice
runners_data.note: Prominent runner rated OR 90, solid recent run of 3rd at this trip on Good going; five runs on similar ground show 0W3P consistency — a reliable each-way type if she secures a forward position cleanly from draw 5.

runners_data.name: Killashee Warrior
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride on this lightly raced 3yo who won on Good going over 8f; 103 days off is a concern though the trainer has a 1/9 14-day strike rate and the booking of Murphy suggests they believe she is fit to run well fresh.

runners_data.name: Tahcawin
runners_data.note: True hold-up operator stepping up slightly in trip from 7f; tongue-strap applied, and six runs on similar going return 1W3P — suited by a fast pace that brings late runners into play but faces the challenge of weaving through 19 runners from draw 19.

runners_data.name: Mayflower
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type but a poor recent form string of five runs without a place at 8f on Good; the headgear note (p) suggests connections are trying to find an answer, yet the evidence of 0W0P on similar ground is discouraging.

runners_data.name: Suzie Songs
runners_data.note: Smart 3yo for G M Lyons and Colin Keane — a double-winner at 7f on Good and well-handicapped at OR 98 stepping back to a mile she has not yet tried; prominent style suits the likely race shape and the Keane booking is always significant in big-field handicaps at Leopardstown.

runners_data.name: Quebec
runners_data.note: Prominent type carrying top weight of 140lbs after a moderate recent run of 5th; the O'Brien yard has excellent 14-day numbers (6/56) but three runs on Good going return 0W0P and the weight burden in a 19-runner field is a significant ask.

runners_data.name: Pink Oxalis
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly ridden by 3lb claimer from draw 18 — the wide draw helps her bypass early traffic; blinkers applied and a 2nd at 8f on Good is the best recent piece of form, though 0W2P on similar going across six recent runs limits confidence.

runners_data.name: Drop Dead Gorgeous
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the mount on this A P O'Brien 3yo — always a significant factor — but the form string of 139589 shows inconsistency and her hold-up style requires a strongly run race to deliver, which this shape provides.

runners_data.name: Mallavelly
runners_data.note: Midfield type who maps well from a low draw (2) for the Lyons yard; tongue-tie applied and two 2nd-place finishes at 7-8f on Good ground give hope, though 0W3P on similar conditions suggests a place is the ceiling here.

runners_data.name: Thrifty Of Digby
runners_data.note: Genuine front-runner and confirmed pace-setter — two wins and five places from nine runs on Good ground make her the most credible lead horse in the race; OR 79 is competitive but she sets the tempo for everyone and may be vulnerable if pressed throughout by Guardian Of Realm.

runners_data.name: Anvika
runners_data.note: Runs in the Lavery yard's colours on just 10 days' rest with a tongue-tie; her natural running style is hold-up but this very deep prominent/lead-heavy field pushes her into a midfield slot she'd prefer anyway — however the 0W2P on similar going and modest OR 71 make a win difficult to envisage.

runners_data.name: Rebel Wave
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard flags Rebel Wave as a genuine danger — Ben Coen on a 3yo filly who has won twice at 7f on Good and placed at 7f on Soft; stepping up to a mile is the key question, and a prominent draw in stall 1 helps her get a clean passage early without fighting for position.

runners_data.name: Tachos
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type from the Weld yard with the most significant piece of recent form — a win over 8f on Good; OR 72 is competitive and tongue-tie/pads combination is notable; suited by a strong gallop but needs things to fall right through the field.

runners_data.name: Bella Colombia
runners_data.note: In-form 5yo who has won twice and placed five times from seven runs on Good ground — the McCreery yard also saddles Rebel Wave, suggesting stable confidence is divided; her natural style is prominent but the overcrowded prominent group means she is effectively racing from midfield, which mutes her effectiveness despite strong recent form of 523113.

runners_data.name: Guardian Of Realm
runners_data.note: Front-runner from the Hogan yard and a confirmed pace-setter — drew stall 13 which is workable; her 2nd at 8f on Standard and a win at 10f on Good show she has ability, but stepping back to a mile and sharing lead duties with Thrifty Of Digby could see her burned out early.

runners_data.name: Marmeladova
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator on just 10 days' rest from a poor run of 0th; 10 runs on Good ground return an aggregate of 2W4P but the most recent form is alarming (12th, 5th, 6th) suggesting she is out of form rather than freshened up.

runners_data.name: Chica Guerrera
runners_data.note: Prominent type ridden by 7lb claimer Reese Holohan — OR 91 is among the higher-rated in the field but all her recent best form has come at 10-12f and the drop to a mile feels like a trip compromise; 0W2P on Good going at today's distances is a flag.

runners_data.name: Electric Beauty
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard's top selection — prominent type on 93 days off, last run on Soft so the step back to Good is better for her; a recent 1st at 9f on Soft and a 2nd at 10f on Good show progressive form, and trainer Mulvany has a 2/19 14-day strike rate suggesting the horse is ready after a break.

runners_data.name: Blue Blue Moon
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 3yo for J P Murtagh and 5lb claimer McGettigan; won at 8f on Good and the stable has a 2/31 14-day record; headgear note (p) applied and draws stall 6 — a prominent runner who could benefit if the pace falters, but experience against older rivals is limited.

races.paceDynamic: Guardian Of Realm and Thrifty Of Digby are the confirmed front-runners, and with eight of nineteen runners wanting prominent positions, the early stages will be genuinely competitive rather than a gentle procession — expect an honest, pressure-on gallop from the outset on this flat Leopardstown mile. The congestion between the two-furlong and three-furlong poles is where this race is most likely to be decided, as rivals bump into traffic at precisely the moment they need to accelerate. This field carries more prominent-type runners than the race shape can accommodate: Guardian Of Realm and Thrifty Of Digby are most likely to actually secure lead positions, while Bella Colombia and Anvika — natural prominent and hold-up types respectively — are effectively pushed into midfield roles they do not naturally fill, reducing their effectiveness. With an honest pace guaranteed and a flat track that does not blunt stamina, the tactical verdict is clear: genuine mid-to-prominent types who can settle just off the pace within the first four, travel economically through the contested middle stages, and produce a sustained finish in the final two furlongs are the beneficiaries — pure hold-up horses launching from deep face an uncomfortably large field to navigate through.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace, Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Guardian Of Realm and Thrifty Of Digby set a genuine gallop and the race unfolds at an even honest tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: The sustained pace stretches the field and rewards those sitting three to five lengths off the lead with a clear passage into the straight, producing a finish dominated by the prominent group who have conserved their energy through the middle section. Suzie Songs, Electric Beauty, and Rebel Wave all have the profile to travel prominently, find a run turning in, and hit the line hard.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Contested Pace Causes Carnage
scenarios.trigger: If the eight prominent-seeking runners fight for position early, creating an overly strong gallop that burns out the front-runners by the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: The pace collapses in the straight, handing late movers a clear opportunity to sweep past weakening leaders in the final furlong. Tahcawin, Drop Dead Gorgeous, and Tachos are true hold-up types with the stamina and profile to benefit from a fast-run, strung-out race.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runners Dictate
scenarios.trigger: If Thrifty Of Digby or Guardian Of Realm steals a few lengths early and the pack misjudges the tempo, allowing the leader to control the fractions.
scenarios.body: A falsely run first half at a canter followed by a sprint from the front suits the horse that has led throughout and can quicken away before closers can wind up their engines. Thrifty Of Digby's recent Leopardstown win and proven front-running record make this a genuine threat, and Guardian Of Realm has similar front-running form credentials.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Chaos, Dark Horse
scenarios.trigger: If severe traffic problems two to three furlongs out produce a fragmented finish where several fancied runners are impeded.
scenarios.body: A horse who finds an improbable gap through a fractured field benefits, and the wide draw of Tahcawin (19) and Pink Oxalis (18) could prove advantageous as they bypass the inner congestion entirely. Mallavelly and Blue Blue Moon, both capable of travelling prominently from low draws, could also profit if rivals are squeezed out.

watchPoints.text: Traffic explosion two to three furlongs out is the single biggest danger in this race — with 8 of 19 runners wanting prominent positions, horses like Bella Colombia and Suzie Songs face genuine risk of being squeezed for room at the crucial moment.

Thrifty Of Digby and Guardian Of Realm will press each other throughout — if neither blinks and they burn each other out in a contested lead battle, the entire front group may collapse simultaneously in the final furlong.
Electric Beauty is the Strand top selection but has not raced in 93 days and all her form on Going Good is limited — watch the market move at the off to gauge stable confidence after the break.

Rebel Wave drops in OR (82) and faces a first attempt at a mile — Ben Coen's positioning from stall 1 in the first two furlongs will be the clearest early signal of whether connections believe she stays the trip.

Bella Colombia and Anvika are both racing effectively out of their natural roles due to field congestion — punters should factor in that their usual tactical advantages are structurally compromised in this specific race shape.
